entities.label: TextOfTheConstitution
entities.rationale: The text of the Constitution is a specific information artifact whose content (the linguistic/normative pattern) can be instantiated in multiple physical copies (parchment, printings, digital files). This is the hallmark of a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031). It is an individual (a particular document content), and it is a kind of Statute as already modeled in the working ontology. The existing individual USConstitution appears to refer to the constitutional document as a whole; TextOfTheConstitution is more precisely the information content (GDC) that is concretized in physical copies.

relations.rationale: The text of the Constitution is an instance of the Statute class, which is already typed as a subclass of BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant) in the working ontology.

The text (information content) is a part of the broader USConstitution individual already in the ontology. The textual content is the generically dependent part that gives the constitution its normative identity.

open_questions: Should 'TextOfTheConstitution' be treated as strictly identical to 'USConstitution' (i.e., the same individual under a different description), or is there a distinction worth preserving between the constitutional document-as-artifact and its textual/normative content as an information object?
Are we modeling a specific national constitution's text (e.g., the US Constitution), or is 'the text of the Constitution' intended generically as a class-level example of constitutional text?
Should a class 'ConstitutionalText' (subclass of Statute or LegalForm) be minted to cover all instances of constitutional texts, with TextOfTheConstitution as one instance?
proposal.rationale_summary: The text of the Constitution is paradigmatically a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031): it is an information pattern that depends for its existence on being concretized in some physical bearer (parchment, paper, digital storage) but is not identical to any single bearer and can be multiply instantiated. It is not a material entity (the physical document would be BFO_0000040), nor a specifically dependent continuant (it is not tied to exactly one bearer). The working ontology already has the class Statute (typed as BFO_0000031) and the individual USConstitution (also BFO_0000031). I model TextOfTheConstitution as a new individual of type Statute, related via BFO_0000050 (part of) to USConstitution, on the reading that the textual content is a proper part of the constitutional document as a whole. Open questions remain about whether this individual should be merged with USConstitution or kept distinct, and whether a ConstitutionalText class should be introduced.
